display: Food technologist at a Singapore polytechnic lab with pilot retort-pouch equipment, working on shelf-stable sauces and pastes.

signals.text: I'm looking for a small local food company that has a real sauce or paste product and wants to make it shelf-stable.
My industry grant needs a registered local commercial partner with a real product by March, and I don't have one yet.
The two food SMEs I've talked to so far had no product ready. The big companies on the old industry day list are the wrong size for me.
My belacan sambal trials keep darkening and losing the shrimp aroma in the retort. Trial 3 has a better colour but a flat aroma.
Trial 3's water activity is 0.89. I need to get it lower or add more preservatives, and I'm not happy with it.
I want to try ascorbic acid against Maillard browning in trial 4, and I'd like to hear from anyone who has done this in retort pouches.
The pilot plant is booked solid with students. I only get Tuesday afternoons, which slows my iterations.
I'm meeting SFA on 20 October about labelling requirements and would like to hear from anyone who has been through shelf-stable sauce labelling.
I want to find belacan or sambal made by hawkers and small makers that is fragrant enough to taste-test against my own.
Our BTO kitchen cabinets are delayed again. We've been eating takeout for three weeks.
I'm planning a Taiwan hike (Alishan, Yushan) from 3 November and would like local tips on weather, gear and logistics.
I'm learning the erhu from my grandmother. My bowing is too stiff, and I'd like to meet other people learning traditional instruments.

offers.text: I can run pouch products through a pilot-scale Steriflow lab retort for process trials and thermal process validation.
I can advise on HACCP, thermal process design, pH and water activity testing for shelf-stable sauces and pastes.
I can run accelerated shelf-life tests (for example 35°C storage) and report colour, aroma and water activity results.
I can use the polytechnic's sensory testing room to run tasting panels on a product.
I can help a small local food company turn a fresh-made sauce into a retort-pouch prototype with a real shelf-life data package.
I have family sambal recipes and hands-on knowledge of how belacan-based sambal behaves under heat.
I have contacts at SFA and among local food SMEs, and can introduce people where it makes sense.
I can explain food safety and retort basics to non-specialists, for example founders who are new to shelf-stable products.

catchers.hypo: I run a small sambal or sauce business in Singapore. My product is made fresh and keeps only a few days. Can it be made shelf-stable without losing flavour?
catchers.can: Run it through retort and shelf-life trials in the polytechnic lab (Tuesday afternoons), and discuss a joint development arrangement.
catchers.confirm: Is your company a registered Singapore business with a product that already sells (not just an idea)?

catchers.hypo: We make a sauce, paste or curry base in Singapore and want to sell it in pouches at room temperature. We have no lab or process validation capability. Who can help?
catchers.can: Provide thermal process validation, pH and water activity testing, and a shelf-life study, and possibly act as a development partner.
catchers.confirm: Is your product a sauce, paste or similar wet product that could be packed in a retort pouch?

catchers.hypo: I'm a food scientist who has tried ascorbic acid or other antioxidants against Maillard browning in retorted shrimp or fermented pastes. Want to compare notes?
catchers.can: Share trial data and swap findings on browning and aroma retention in retort pouches.
catchers.confirm: Have you worked on browning or aroma loss specifically in retort-processed, shrimp- or fish-based products?

catchers.hypo: I want to learn the erhu, and I'm looking for a patient teacher in Singapore who can teach traditional style rather than exam pieces.
catchers.can: Introduce them to her grandmother, who teaches erhu, if the fit is right.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for lessons in traditional erhu playing, and can you do them in person in Singapore?

catchers.hypo: I'm a belacan maker or hawker with a very fragrant product and I'd like to find out how to keep it longer without losing the aroma.
catchers.can: Test the product's pH, water activity and keeping quality in the lab, and talk through preservation options.
catchers.confirm: Do you make your own belacan or sambal and want it to last months rather than days?

catchers.hypo: I'm a student or small startup founder who wants to understand how to validate a shelf-stable sauce for safety. Where do I start?
catchers.can: Explain HACCP, pH, water activity and thermal process basics, and point to the right regulatory steps with SFA.
catchers.confirm: Are you at the stage of planning or prototyping, not yet asking for large-scale commercial production?

catchers.hypo: I run a small kitchen cabinet workshop in Singapore and have capacity to fit a BTO kitchen within the next few weeks.
catchers.can: Talk to Mei Ling about a replacement for her delayed cabinets.
catchers.confirm: Can you deliver and install a full BTO kitchen cabinet set within three weeks?

catchers.hypo: I've hiked Alishan and Yushan in early November and can tell you about permits, weather and trail conditions.
catchers.can: Use the tips for her November trip and possibly trade hiking advice.
catchers.confirm: Have you hiked Yushan or Alishan yourself in the last two years?

forbids.text: I can't use the lab's equipment for commercial production at scale. It is for development and validation only.
The grant requires the commercial partner to be a registered local company, so I can't count overseas or unregistered businesses.
I can only use the pilot plant on Tuesday afternoons, so I can't promise quick turnaround on trials.
I will be away hiking in Taiwan from 3 November, so I can't take on anything time-critical then.

projects.name: Shelf-stable sambal
projects.text: Develop a belacan-based sambal that keeps 12 months at room temperature in a retort pouch, with its aroma and colour intact.
roles_needed: food SME that could commercialise it

projects.name: Local SME shelf-stable product partnership
projects.text: Work with a registered Singapore food company on a real sauce or paste product, using the polytechnic's retort and testing capacity, to produce validated shelf-life data by March.
roles_needed: registered local food SME with a real product

policy.t1: When there is a real signal, I'll share that my industry grant needs a commercial partner with a real product by March, and details about my sambal project and lab access.
policy.t2: Once I'm fairly sure of the fit and know who you are, I'll talk about how the grant situation worries me.
policy.never: My personal finances, and anything about my lab director's knowledge of my partner search.
